behavior.rule: [self-critique] Hard rule: zero empty turns — if stuck, re-poll job_output, re-issue a failed call with one field corrected, or fire a coverage_check on a new vuln_class; any concrete call beats silence
[self-critique] Pair every background terminal with a job_output within 2 steps; never launch work you won't harvest before synthesis
[self-critique] After any tool FAIL, diff my args against the error message on the very next call and freeze the working schema in working memory — no reverts
[self-critique] Treat each coverage_check FAIL as a queued probe: enumerate the missing vuln_class values and convert each into exactly one concrete action
[self-critique] Set a personal dead-call threshold: if 2 consecutive tool invocations return empty, STOP using that tool and switch modality entirely (terminal → HTTP → different approach)
[self-critique] Sequence: recon → attack_tree → targeted probing → report. Never generate the report and then keep making requests — if new data arrives post-report, the report is already stale
[self-critique] mesh_broadcast is only useful if I verify peer count first — otherwise it's a wasted turn on a solo engagement

[self-critique] Run cheapest disqualifiers first on any lead: DNS resolution before subdomain enumeration, body-level service status before leaked-key exploitation, known-interstitial check before public re
[self-critique] At any redirect or auth boundary, pair the encoding matrix with HPP, case tricks, and sibling wildcard-DNS resolvers — encodings alone are an incomplete test matrix.

[self-critique] On signed-token bugs, always test replay and mint as separate hypotheses, and hunt public archives for pre-rotation tokens to size real exposure — never accept 'expiry mitigates it' without
[self-critique] Treat every JSONP endpoint as a family: enumerate all front-ends and probe callback filters with homoglyphs/escapes, not just the canonical identifier charset.
[self-critique] Grep the workspace for artifacts from prior engagements before trusting any flag or credential string — contamination costs one command on day one and an entire lane on day three.
[self-critique] The instant creds_add succeeds, the next call must be scope/privilege validation (list projects, test service APIs) — credentials unused are credentials unproven
[self-critique] Deduplicate by hashing tool+args before dispatch; identical digests (like my two key probes) should never both fire
[self-critique] Hard rule: if two consecutive turns produce no new findings, change tactic — never emit filler calls to fill quota
[self-critique] generate_report is a terminal operation; calling it mid-run should trip an alarm, not pass silently

[self-critique] On mega-scope single-domain targets, findings cluster in shared endpoint plumbing: once one redirect/auth flaw validates, enumerate the entire sibling family (all minters, all redirect sinks

[self-critique] Fix the tool contract first, retry second — one schema lookup beats two failed arg-order swaps; and when a discovery tool (surface_expand) fails, the resulting coverage hole must be an expli
[self-critique] Verify leaked-key impact at the enforcement layer (API restrictions/allowlists), never at the console page — the K1/K2 treatment is the reusable pattern
[self-critique] Namespace/scope-tag every artifact at capture time; catching the FLAG{northbridge...} contamination saved a false positive and should be standing procedure on multi-engagement nodes
